properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 15 at 3:29AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
At 328 AM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Durango, moving east at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation and
outdoor objects is possible.

Locations impacted include...
Durango.

This includes the following highways...
U.S. Highway 550 in Colorado between mile markers 21 and 29.
U.S. Highway 160 in Colorado between mile markers 75 and 85, and
between mile markers 90 and 98.
Colorado 172 near mile marker 24.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.
properties.area: Southwest San Juan Mountains; Animas River Basin

properties.title: Flood Watch issued September 15 at 4:19AM CDT until September 15 at 12:00PM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Des Moines has issued a Flood
Watch for the following rivers in Iowa...

Walnut Creek at Des Moines 63rd St affecting Polk County.

* WHAT...Flooding is possible.

* WHERE...Walnut Creek at Des Moines 63rd St, or from 1 1/3 miles
upstream of North Walnut Creek to the Raccoon River.

* WHEN...From early this morning to this afternoon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:01 AM CDT Tuesday the stage was 12.1 feet, and rising.
- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached based on the latest
forecast information.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
If you are in the watch area, remain alert to possible flooding.

For the latest stream observations and forecasts refer to
weather.gov/desmoines/water.

River forecasts include observed precipitation plus forecast
precipitation over the next 24 hours.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 3:01AM CDT until September 15 at 9:00AM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
FFWDMX

The National Weather Service in Des Moines has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Dallas County in central Iowa...
Northwestern Madison County in south central Iowa...
Northern Adair County in southwestern Iowa...
Northern Cass County in southwestern Iowa...
Southern Audubon County in west central Iowa...
Southern Guthrie County in west central Iowa...

* Until 900 AM CDT.

* At 301 AM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicate
additional thunderstorms will produce heavy rain across the warned
area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned area.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges indicate 1 to 3 inches have
fallen, with more thunderstorms moving into the area.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Atlantic, Stuart, Earlham, Anita, Exira, Redfield, Adair, Dexter,
Casey, Diamondhead Lake, Menlo, Linden, Brayton, Marne, Wiota,
Anita Municipal Airport, Lake Anita State Park and Atlantic
Municipal Airport.

This includes Interstate 80 between mile markers 100 and 106...and
between mile markers 50 and 99.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

For the latest stream observations and forecasts refer to
weather.gov/desmoines/water.
properties.area: Adair, IA; Audubon, IA; Cass, IA; Dallas, IA; Guthrie, IA; Madison, IA

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 14 at 9:25PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy
Counties.

.Elevated water levels are expected along the river over the next
several days due to recent heavy rainfall.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 PM EDT Monday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue rising to 28.2 feet just
after midnight tonight. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.4
feet on 08/05/2024.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday afternoon at 200 PM EDT.
properties.area: Citrus, FL; Levy, FL; Marion, FL

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 14 at 9:23PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Tampa Bay Ruskin has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Monday the stage was 9.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
Wednesday morning and continue rising to 12.4 feet Thursday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.5
feet on 08/31/2002.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
